 Period piece … The Gilded Age. Photograph: HBO View image in fullscreen Period piece … The Gilded Age. Photograph: HBO TV tonight Television TV tonight: The Gilded Age returns in all its glossy Julian Fellowes’ glory
 High-society plotting is afoot as nouveau riche arrivistes threaten the old order. Plus, David Harewood’s dogged Pierre won’t let a spot of angina slow him down. Here’s what to watch this evening
 Phil Harrison , Hollie Richardson , Jack Seale and Graeme Virtue Mon 2 Nov 2026 01.15 EST Last modified on Mon 2 Nov 2026 03.06 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The Gilded Age
 9pm, Sky Atlantic 
 Julian Fellowes’ glossy, airy period confection returns. The Gilded Age has now happily embraced its own lack of real nutritional value and, towards the end of the third season, its ratings swelled as a result. In the opener, Agnes is scheming to retain her position in society and there’s a subplot of real modern resonance as old money starts being threatened by crass, arriviste monopolists. Phil Harrison 
 A Place in the Sun
 6pm, Channel 4 
 Now that it’s dark before dinnertime, the show about upping sticks from the UK feels like perfect vicarious viewing. The Dordogne and a gorgeous Greek island feature later in the week but the new run kicks off with a couple contemplating retirement on the balmy Costa Blanca. What can a £450k budget get them? Graeme Virtue 
 Escaping Idi Amin
 9pm, BBC Two 
 In the context of the current hysteria around migration, this two-part documentary has been sobering . As it concludes, it’s 1972 and a month after Uganda’s swaggering dictator Idi Amin issued an ultimatum to the country’s Asian population. They must leave within 90 days, taking nothing more than one suitcase and £50 each. Will Britain take them? PH 
 View image in fullscreen Dogged … David Harewood in Pierre. Photograph: Channel 4 / Olly Courtney Pierre
 9pm, Channel 4 
 It’s the penultimate chapter of David Harewood’s suave legal drama, and if you think collapsing would keep this dogged duty solicitor down, think again (“It wasn’t a heart attack, it was angina”). He escapes his hospital bed to get back on the case following a new lead on Michael’s death. Hollie Richardson 
 Trauma: My Broken Brain
 10pm, Channel 4 
 The documentary’s concluding half follows Dan, Saskia and Dec – all in their 20s – as they recover from life-threatening strokes. As Dan endures surgery to repair a hole in his skull, Saskia goes to great lengths to overcome her neurological fatigue. Dec, meanwhile, finds his psychological recovery more challenging than the physical. Jack Seale 
 Dispatches: The Taliban’s War on Women
 11pm, Channel 4 
 The 2021 US and UK withdrawal from Afghanistan, allowing the Taliban to take control, felt like a shameful betrayal. And the stories that emerge from this remarkable Dispatches documentary confirm that impression. It follows Afghans in exile as they attempt to rescue loved ones from the theocracy; a story of torture, sexual violence, erasure and extraordinary courage. PH
